newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Nineteen die in latest wave of Colombian violence.
newsitem.headline: Nineteen die in latest wave of Colombian violence.

text.p: At least 19 people were killed in the latest wave of violence across Colombia, including eight youths gunned down in a gangland-style massacre at dawn on Saturday outside the city of Medellin, authorities said.
The youths, ranging between 15 and 20 years old, were shot and killed at about 3:30 a.m. (0830 GMT) inside a house in El Picacho, a working-class district on the outskirts of Medellin, police said.
A group of about 10 gunmen travelling in two cars was responsible for the massacre, which was apparently a "settling of accounts" between rival street gangs, a police spokesman said.
He said the victims were all believed to have been members of a gang known as "El Moro" but further details were not immediately available.
Medellin, capital of northwestern Antioquia province, has Colombia's highest rate of violent crime and has often been described as the murder capital of the world.
Two people were killed elsewhere in Antioquia, in the notoriously violent banana-growing region known as Uraba, in an attack late on Friday by unidentified gunmen, police and military officials said.
They said four other people, including a policeman, were killed in an overnight attack by leftist rebels on the small town of Tierra Alta in neighbouring Cordoba province.

The rebels belonged to the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) guerrilla movement. Five FARC rebels were killed in a clash with the military on Friday afternoon in northern Bolivar province, spokesmen for the armed forces said.
